column1: # One vocabulary for every run before a scorer sees it: each word on the left is rewritten to the word on the right.
# Tab-separated columns: old, new, where, and optionally the arms the line applies to (none given: every arm).
#   kind   rewritten wherever the word stands, also in the "why" text, also with a final s, also capitalised
#   field  rewritten only where it stands as a field: in a code span, after a dot, or before "->", "->>" or ":".
#          The plain English word ("by default", "this satisfies") is left alone.
# Only true 1:1 renames are here. `satisfies` is A's `by` in C0 and C only: in B it is another field (offered on
# behaviour kinds only, next to `rule.constrains`), so B's `satisfies` is never rewritten.
# Not mapped, so still visible to a scorer: `many`, `heard`, `realizes` on a capability, the types `one` and `list`
# (A), and everything B adds (`interface` and its fields, `constrains`); B is scored in batches of its own.
# Checked against B's map (43f15fc): stages 2 and 3 bring no 1:1 rename, so nothing was added for B.
